title: The Role of Electron Correlations in Chirality Induced Spin Selectivity of Molecular Junctions
authors: A. Konidena, J. Fransson, L. Kantorovich
abstract: The Non-Equilibrium Green's Function (NEGF) approach is applied to a chain of Hubbard atoms in a helical geometry sandwiched between two leads, one of which is magnetic, to assess what role the electronic correlation effects within the molecule may play in explaining the Chirality Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) effect. The correlation effects are treated at the level of the self-consistent second Born approximation. Two chiralities, Laevorotatory (L) and Dextrorotatory (D), of the helix, are discussed. Further, we account for spin-orbit coupling (SOC) within the chains using a simplified model of Kane and Mele that exploits next-nearest neighbour interactions intrinsic to a curved geometry. The interaction with the leads is considered within the Wide Band Approximation. We consider the ratio, U/t, of the Hubbard constant U to the hopping t between atomic sites along the chain of up to two, but found very little spin polarisation in our calculations. Even though the spin polarisation factor defined as a relative difference between the largest and smallest total current is found for both enantiomers practically the same, the orientation of the tip's polarisation required to reach the largest and smallest currents for the two enantiomers differed. It is also found that the qualitative agreement with observations can only be achieved if we account, self-consistently, for the second order of the perturbation theory. The distribution of the spin populations on the chain atoms for different U/t ratios is also discussed. This study concludes that even though accounting for electron-electron interactions are important in understanding spin selectivity within molecular junctions, they cannot be made solely responsible for the high spin polarisation factors observed in experiments.
summary: This theoretical study investigates whether electron-electron correlations are the primary cause of the Chirality Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) effect in molecular junctions. Using the NEGF method with Hubbard atoms, the authors found that while correlations are important, they alone cannot account for the large spin polarization factors seen in experiments. The results suggest that other mechanisms, beyond simple correlation effects, must be at play.
main_problem: The study aims to determine the specific role of electronic correlation effects in explaining the Chirality Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) effect in molecular junctions.
main_result: The calculations found very little spin polarization, suggesting that while electron-electron interactions are important for spin selectivity, they cannot be solely responsible for the high polarization factors observed experimentally.
method: The Non-Equilibrium Green's Function (NEGF) approach is employed, treating correlation effects using the self-consistent second Born approximation.
model_or_system: The physical system modeled is a chain of Hubbard atoms arranged in a helical geometry, sandwiched between two leads, one of which is magnetic.
key_observables: Spin polarization (SP) factor, total currents for different spin directions, and the distribution of spin populations on the chain atoms.
important_parameters: The ratio of the Hubbard constant to the hopping parameter ($U/t$), and the strength of spin-orbit coupling (SOC).
main_assumptions: The interaction with the leads is treated within the Wide Band Approximation, and correlation effects are systematically included up to the second Born approximation.
paper_structure: The paper systematically applies the NEGF formalism to model spin transport through a chiral molecular junction, comparing results for L and D enantiomers while varying the correlation strength ($U/t$).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses spin transport in nanoscale systems using advanced many-body techniques (NEGF, SBA), which is highly relevant to open quantum systems and molecular spintronics.
